page: Vultr vcg-a16-96c-960g-256vram is a bare metal server belonging to the Dedicated Metal GPU family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel CPU with 96 dedicated vCPUs. The system is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 1700 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Although classified under the Dedicated Metal GPU family with NVIDIA listed as the GPU manufacturer, the active GPU count for this specific configuration is 0.0.

Due to the high memory allocation of 960.0 GB relative to the 96 dedicated Intel vCPUs, this server offers significant resource density for memory-intensive workloads. The inclusion of high-speed NVMe SSD local storage supports fast data access, though specific benchmark performance data is unavailable for this instance type. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated bare-metal allocation of both compute and memory resources eliminates virtualization overhead, making it suitable for large-scale databases, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise-grade workloads requiring isolated, high-capacity hardware.
